The one thing that matters most

Anthropic renamed its Claude plans: Max 5x is now Max ($100 a month) and Max 20x is now Ultra ($200 a month), and verified Ultra accounts no longer have the five-hour usage limit.

Existing subscribers switch automatically. Also big: Google says it booted an AI chip on a satellite in orbit, sent it a prompt and got a haiku back, and Testing Catalog reports the first stable Grok Bot version is out.

Claude@claudeai
We’re renaming our Max plans:

Max 5x → Max
Max 20x → Ultra

Max is still $100/month, and Ultra is still $200. If you’re a subscriber, there’s nothing you need to do.

We’re also removing the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts, starting today with most existing subscribers. Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until they’re verified, which helps us prevent fraud and abuse. You'll get an email when it's removed.

I see a lot of confusion around the new Claude Ultra plan concerning the new 10x usage.

Worth clarifying 👀

Claude Max 20x (old plan)
- 5-hour session allowance - 20x Pro

Claude Ultra (new plan)

- Weekly allowance - 10x Pro
mike overell@mboverell· Oct 30
I lead product for Claude subscriptions. Today we're renaming our Max plans, and I want to explain why.

When we launched our top plan in April 2025, it had a single limit: 5 hours. It gave you 20x Pro's limit, so we called it Max 20x. When we added weekly limits to Max 20x, we set them to 10x Pro's (the 5-hour limit stayed at 20x).

I get that some new users assumed 20x applied to both limits. We could have done better here, and I'm sorry.

The Ultra plan keeps the weekly limit (10x Pro), but we're removing the 5-hour limit so you can keep building without getting blocked mid-session. This starts today and rolls out in stages. To help prevent fraud and abuse, a temporary limit applies until we've verified your account. You'll get an email when your limit is removed.

We've got more cooking and can't wait to share it. Thanks for building with Claude 🙏

Rock Matrix open-sourced EdgeRock-4B, a small text-and-image reasoning model with fixed-size memory.

🚨 AI News | TestingCatalog@testingcatalog
Rock Matrix has open-sourced EdgeRock-4B, a small text-and-image reasoning model with fixed-capacity memory.

EdgeRock-4B keeps its attention KV cache fixed in size by holding the last 1,024 tokens in full and saving important older details to a separate bank.

Standard language models keep a growing record of every token they read, so long chats and long reasoning take up more GPU memory over time. 

Rock Matrix reports an 82.9% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024–2026, compared to 18.8% for the strongest bounded-state model it tested.

Siemens used NVIDIA NeMo Gym to make its chip-design agent more reliable by checking the files it produced and tracing errors.

NVIDIA AI@NVIDIAAI
How do you make a chip design agent more reliable and efficient?

The @Siemens EDA team used NVIDIA NeMo Gym to check the engineering files its agent produced, trace errors, and improve the agent’s skills and tool descriptions.

In its standard cell characterization benchmark, those changes raised the composite verification score from ~55% to ~95%, with 66% fewer agent turns and 64% fewer output tokens.

We just published a new techblog that walks through what the team measured, what they changed, and how other engineering teams can apply the approach → nvda.ws/4Beujcb
